label: prf:h3-markov-wenzl-weights
title: Proof of h3 markov wenzl weights
html:
Proof. Proof of h3 markov wenzl weights

Proof. Three steps, each forced.

Step 1 — y_{(1^3)} \equiv 0 (Temperley–Lieb quotient). The Jones polynomial factors through the Temperley–Lieb algebra \mathrm{TL}_n(q) (Kauffman bracket), which is the quotient of \mathrm{H}_n(q) annihilating every V_\lambda with more than two rows. For n = 3 the only such partition is (1^3), so the Jones-normalised Markov trace assigns it weight zero identically in q. Equivalently, the vanishing is the algebraic identity

  [2]_q^{3} - 2\,[2]_q - [4]_q \;=\; 0,

verified by direct expansion: with [2]_q = q + q^{-1}, [2]_q^3 = q^3 + 3q + 3q^{-1} + q^{-3}, so [2]_q^3 - 2[2]_q = q^3 + q + q^{-1} + q^{-3} = [4]_q.

Step 2 — Markov normalisation. \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathbf{1}_3) = 1 (the identity braid closes to the 3-component unlink, whose Jones value is exactly the normalising [2]_q^2). With d_{(3)}, d_{(2,1)}, d_{(1^3)} = 1, 2, 1 and Step 1:

  y_{(3)}(q) + 2\, y_{(2,1)}(q) \;=\; 1.

Step 3 — uniqueness from the Borromean closed form. For \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} (writhe 0, image \mathrm{id} \in S_3), \chi^{(3)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) = 1 exactly and \chi^{(2,1)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) = 2 - 3h^4 - h^6 with h = q - q^{-1}. Substituting Steps 1–2:

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}})
  \;=\;
  1 + y_{(2,1)}(q)\,\bigl(\chi^{(2,1)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) - 2\bigr)
  \;=\;
  1 - y_{(2,1)}(q)\,\bigl(3h^4 + h^6\bigr).

Comparing with the closed form \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) = (4 + h^2 - 3h^4 - h^6)/(h^2+4) = 1 - (3h^4 + h^6)/(h^2 + 4), and noting 3h^4 + h^6 \neq 0 for h \neq 0:

  y_{(2,1)}(q) \;=\; \frac{1}{h^2 + 4} \;=\; \frac{1}{[2]_q^{2}}
  \qquad\text{(uniquely, for all } q \neq 1\text{; at } q = 1 \text{ by continuity)}.

Then Step 2 gives y_{(3)} = 1 - 2/[2]_q^2 = ([2]_q^2 - 2)/[2]_q^2 = [4]_q / [2]_q^3 using Step 1's identity. \square

Direction of the argument. Step 3 determines y_{(2,1)} from the Borromean closed form, which is itself a convention-D object. The step is therefore a consistency computation internal to convention D, and it is not evidence for selecting D over the full-Hecke Ocneanu trace (convention C) in any channel — using it that way would be circular. The independent characterisation of D is the Temperley–Lieb uniqueness argument (y_{(1^3)}(z) = 0 has the unique non-degenerate root z = q^3/(q^2+1); QOU.BraidsAndKnots.MarkovTraceTLUniqueness), whose premise — that the relevant fibre functor lands in \mathrm{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)) \simeq \mathrm{TL}_3 — is a separate question. See the trace-convention registry.
